NASB.1: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came to the land of the sons of the east.
NASB.2: He looked, and saw a well in the field, and behold, three flocks of sheep were lying there beside it, for from that well they watered the flocks. Now the stone on the mouth of the well was large.
NASB.3: When all the flocks were gathered there, they would then roll the stone from the mouth of the well and water the sheep, and put the stone back in its place on the mouth of the well.
NASB.4: Jacob said to them, 'My brothers, where are you from?' And they said, 'We are from Haran.'
NASB.5: He said to them, 'Do you know Laban the son of Nahor?' And they said, 'We know [him].'
NASB.6: And he said to them, 'Is it well with him?' And they said, 'It is well, and here is Rachel his daughter coming with the sheep.'
NASB.7: He said, 'Behold, it is still high day; it is not time for the livestock to be gathered. Water the sheep, and go, pasture them.'
NASB.8: But they said, 'We cannot, until all the flocks are gathered, and they roll the stone from the mouth of the well; then we water the sheep.'
NASB.9: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, for she was a shepherdess.
NASB.10: When Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban his mother's brother, and the sheep of Laban his mother's brother, Jacob went up and rolled the stone from the mouth of the well and watered the flock of Laban his mother's brother.
NASB.11: Then Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted his voice and wept.
NASB.12: Jacob told Rachel that he was a relative of her father and that he was Rebekah's son, and she ran and told her father.
NASB.13: So when Laban heard the news of Jacob his sister's son, he ran to meet him, and embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his house. Then he related to Laban all these things.
NASB.14: Laban said to him, 'Surely you are my bone and my flesh.' And he stayed with him a month.
NASB.15: Then Laban said to Jacob, 'Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?'
NASB.16: Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
NASB.17: And Leah's eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful of form and face.
NASB.18: Now Jacob loved Rachel, so he said, 'I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.'
NASB.19: Laban said, 'It is better that I give her to you than to give her to another man; stay with me.'
NASB.20: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel and they seemed to him but a few days because of his love for her.
NASB.21: Then Jacob said to Laban, 'Give [me] my wife, for my time is completed, that I may go in to her.'
NASB.22: Laban gathered all the men of the place and made a feast.
NASB.23: Now in the evening he took his daughter Leah, and brought her to him; and [Jacob] went in to her.
NASB.24: Laban also gave his maid Zilpah to his daughter Leah as a maid.
NASB.25: So it came about in the morning that, behold, it was Leah! And he said to Laban, 'What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel that I served with you? Why then have you deceived me?'
NASB.26: But Laban said, 'It is not the practice in our place to marry off the younger before the firstborn.
NASB.27: 'Complete the week of this one, and we will give you the other also for the service which you shall serve with me for another seven years.'
NASB.28: Jacob did so and completed her week, and he gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
NASB.29: Laban also gave his maid Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her maid.
NASB.30: So [Jacob] went in to Rachel also, and indeed he loved Rachel more than Leah, and he served with Laban for another seven years.
NASB.31: Now the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, and He opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.
NASB.32: Leah conceived and bore a son and named him Reuben, for she said, 'Because the LORD has seen my affliction; surely now my husband will love me.'
NASB.33: Then she conceived again and bore a son and said, 'Because the LORD has heard that I am unloved, He has therefore given me this [son] also.' So she named him Simeon.
NASB.34: She conceived again and bore a son and said, 'Now this time my husband will become attached to me, because I have borne him three sons.' Therefore he was named Levi.
NASB.35: And she conceived again and bore a son and said, 'This time I will praise the LORD.' Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.

NKJV.1: So Jacob went on his journey and came to the land of the people of the East.
NKJV.2: And he looked, and saw a well in the field; and behold, there were three flocks of sheep lying by it; for out of that well they watered the flocks. A large stone was on the well’s mouth.
NKJV.3: Now all the flocks would be gathered there; and they would roll the stone from the well’s mouth, water the sheep, and put the stone back in its place on the well’s mouth.
NKJV.4: And Jacob said to them, “My brethren, where are you from?” And they said, “We are from Haran.”
NKJV.5: Then he said to them, “Do you know Laban the son of Nahor?” And they said, “We know him.”
NKJV.6: So he said to them, “Is he well?” And they said, “He is well. And look, his daughter Rachel is coming with the sheep.”
NKJV.7: Then he said, “Look, it is still high day; it is not time for the cattle to be gathered together. Water the sheep, and go and feed them.”
NKJV.8: But they said, “We cannot until all the flocks are gathered together, and they have rolled the stone from the well’s mouth; then we water the sheep.”
NKJV.9: Now while he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

NKJV.11: Then Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice and wept.
NKJV.12: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s relative and that he was Rebekah’s son. So she ran and told her father.

NKJV.14: And Laban said to him, “Surely you are my bone and my flesh.” And he stayed with him for a month.
NKJV.15: Then Laban said to Jacob, “Because you are my relative, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what should your wages be?”
NKJV.16: Now Laban had two daughters: the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
NKJV.17: Leah’s eyes were delicate, but Rachel was beautiful of form and appearance.
NKJV.18: Now Jacob loved Rachel; so he said, “I will serve you seven years for Rachel your younger daughter.”
NKJV.19: And Laban said, “It is better that I give her to you than that I should give her to another man. Stay with me.”
NKJV.20: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed only a few days to him because of the love he had for her.
NKJV.21: Then Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her.”
NKJV.22: And Laban gathered together all the men of the place and made a feast.
NKJV.23: Now it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter and brought her to Jacob; and he went in to her.
NKJV.24: And Laban gave his maid Zilpah to his daughter Leah as a maid.
NKJV.25: So it came to pass in the morning, that behold, it was Leah. And he said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? Was it not for Rachel that I served you? Why then have you deceived me?”
NKJV.26: And Laban said, “It must not be done so in our country, to give the younger before the firstborn.
NKJV.27: Fulfill her week, and we will give you this one also for the service which you will serve with me still another seven years.”
NKJV.28: Then Jacob did so and fulfilled her week. So he gave him his daughter Rachel as wife also.
NKJV.29: And Laban gave his maid Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as a maid.
NKJV.30: Then Jacob also went in to Rachel, and he also loved Rachel more than Leah. And he served with Laban still another seven years.
NKJV.31: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
NKJV.32: So Leah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Reuben; for she said, “The LORD has surely looked on my affliction. Now therefore, my husband will love me.”
NKJV.33: Then she conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am unloved, He has therefore given me this son also.” And she called his name Simeon.
NKJV.34: She conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Now this time my husband will become attached to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore his name was called Levi.
NKJV.35: And she conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Now I will praise the LORD.” Therefore she called his name Judah. Then she stopped bearing.

NLT.1: Then Jacob hurried on, finally arriving in the land of the east.
NLT.2: He saw a well in the distance. Three flocks of sheep and goats lay in an open field beside it, waiting to be watered. But a heavy stone covered the mouth of the well.
NLT.3: It was the custom there to wait for all the flocks to arrive before removing the stone and watering the animals. Afterward the stone would be placed back over the mouth of the well.
NLT.4: Jacob went over to the shepherds and asked, “Where are you from, my friends?” “We are from Haran,” they answered.
NLT.5: “Do you know a man there named Laban, the grandson of Nahor?” he asked. “Yes, we do,” they replied.
NLT.6: “Is he doing well?” Jacob asked. “Yes, he’s well,” they answered. “Look, here comes his daughter Rachel with the flock now.”
NLT.7: Jacob said, “Look, it’s still broad daylight — too early to round up the animals. Why don’t you water the sheep and goats so they can get back out to pasture?”
NLT.8: “We can’t water the animals until all the flocks have arrived,” they replied. “Then the shepherds move the stone from the mouth of the well, and we water all the sheep and goats.”
NLT.9: Jacob was still talking with them when Rachel arrived with her father’s flock, for she was a shepherd.
NLT.10: And because Rachel was his cousin — the daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother — and because the sheep and goats belonged to his uncle Laban, Jacob went over to the well and moved the stone from its mouth and watered his uncle’s flock.
NLT.11: Then Jacob kissed Rachel, and he wept aloud.
NLT.12: He explained to Rachel that he was her cousin on her father’s side — the son of her aunt Rebekah. So Rachel quickly ran and told her father, Laban.
NLT.13: As soon as Laban heard that his nephew Jacob had arrived, he ran out to meet him. He embraced and kissed him and brought him home. When Jacob had told him his story,
NLT.14: Laban exclaimed, “You really are my own flesh and blood!” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had stayed with Laban for about a month,
NLT.15: Laban said to him, “You shouldn’t work for me without pay just because we are relatives. Tell me how much your wages should be.”
NLT.16: Now Laban had two daughters. The older daughter was named Leah, and the younger one was Rachel.
NLT.17: There was no sparkle in Leah’s eyes, but Rachel had a beautiful figure and a lovely face.
NLT.18: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he told her father, “I’ll work for you for seven years if you’ll give me Rachel, your younger daughter, as my wife.”
NLT.19: “Agreed!” Laban replied. “I’d rather give her to you than to anyone else. Stay and work with me.”
NLT.20: So Jacob worked seven years to pay for Rachel. But his love for her was so strong that it seemed to him but a few days.
NLT.21: Finally, the time came for him to marry her. “I have fulfilled my agreement,” Jacob said to Laban. “Now give me my wife so I can sleep with her.”
NLT.22: So Laban invited everyone in the neighborhood and prepared a wedding feast.
NLT.23: But that night, when it was dark, Laban took Leah to Jacob, and he slept with her.
NLT.24: (Laban had given Leah a servant, Zilpah, to be her maid.)
NLT.25: But when Jacob woke up in the morning — it was Leah! “What have you done to me?” Jacob raged at Laban. “I worked seven years for Rachel! Why have you tricked me?”
NLT.26: “It’s not our custom here to marry off a younger daughter ahead of the firstborn,” Laban replied.
NLT.27: “But wait until the bridal week is over; then we’ll give you Rachel, too — provided you promise to work another seven years for me.”
NLT.28: So Jacob agreed to work seven more years. A week after Jacob had married Leah, Laban gave him Rachel, too.
NLT.29: (Laban gave Rachel a servant, Bilhah, to be her maid.)
NLT.30: So Jacob slept with Rachel, too, and he loved her much more than Leah. He then stayed and worked for Laban the additional seven years.
NLT.31: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, he enabled her to have children, but Rachel could not conceive.
NLT.32: So Leah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She named him Reuben, for she said, “The LORD has noticed my misery, and now my husband will love me.”
NLT.33: She soon became pregnant again and gave birth to another son. She named him Simeon, for she said, “The LORD heard that I was unloved and has given me another son.”
NLT.34: Then she became pregnant a third time and gave birth to another son. He was named Levi, for she said, “Surely this time my husband will feel affection for me, since I have given him three sons!”
NLT.35: Once again Leah became pregnant and gave birth to another son. She named him Judah, for she said, “Now I will praise the LORD!” And then she stopped having children.

CSB17.1: Jacob resumed his journey <sup>[1]</sup> and went to the eastern country. <sup>[2]</sup> <sup>ⓛ</sup>
CSB17.2: He looked and saw a well in a field. Three flocks of sheep were lying there beside it because the sheep were watered from this well. But a large stone covered the opening of the well.
CSB17.3: The shepherds would roll the stone from the opening of the well and water the sheep when all the flocks <sup>[3]</sup> were gathered there. Then they would return the stone to its place over the well’s opening.
CSB17.4: Jacob asked the men at the well, “My brothers! Where are you from?” “We’re from Haran,” they answered.
CSB17.5: “Do you know Laban grandson of Nahor?” Jacob asked them. They answered, “We know him.”
CSB17.6: “Is he well?” Jacob asked. “Yes,” they said, “and here is his daughter Rachel, coming with his sheep.”
CSB17.7: Then Jacob said, “Look, it is still broad daylight. It’s not time for the animals to be gathered. Water the flock, then go out and let them graze.”
CSB17.8: But they replied, “We can’t until all the flocks have been gathered and the stone is rolled from the well’s opening. Then we will water the sheep.”
CSB17.9: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.
CSB17.10: As soon as Jacob saw his uncle Laban’s daughter Rachel with his sheep, <sup>[4]</sup> he went up and rolled the stone from the opening and watered his uncle Laban’s sheep.
CSB17.11: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and wept loudly. <sup>[5]</sup>
CSB17.12: He told Rachel that he was her father’s relative, Rebekah’s son. She ran and told her father.
CSB17.13: When Laban heard the news about his sister’s son Jacob, he ran to meet him, hugged him, and kissed him. Then he took him to his house, and Jacob told him all that had happened.
CSB17.14: Laban said to him, “Yes, you are my own flesh and blood.” <sup>[6]</sup> <sup>ⓜ</sup> After Jacob had stayed with him a month,
CSB17.15: Laban said to him, “Just because you’re my relative, should you work for me for nothing? Tell me what your wages should be.”
CSB17.16: Now Laban had two daughters: the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.
CSB17.17: Leah had tender eyes, but Rachel was shapely and beautiful.
CSB17.18: Jacob loved Rachel, so he answered Laban, “I’ll work for you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.” <sup>ⓝ</sup>
CSB17.19: Laban replied, “Better that I give her to you than to some other man. Stay with me.”
CSB17.20: So Jacob worked seven years for Rachel, and they seemed like only a few days to him because of his love for her.
CSB17.21: Then Jacob said to Laban, “Since my time is complete, give me my wife, so I can sleep with <sup>[7]</sup> her.”
CSB17.22: So Laban invited all the men of the place and sponsored a feast.
CSB17.23: That evening, Laban took his daughter Leah and gave her to Jacob, and he slept with her.
CSB17.24: And Laban gave his slave Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her slave.
CSB17.25: When morning came, there was Leah! So he said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? Wasn’t it for Rachel that I worked for you? Why have you deceived me?”
CSB17.26: Laban answered, “It is not the custom in this place to give the younger daughter in marriage before the firstborn.
CSB17.27: Complete this week of wedding celebration, and we will also give you this younger one in return for working yet another seven years for me.”
CSB17.28: And Jacob did just that. He finished the week of celebration, and Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his wife.
CSB17.29: And Laban gave his slave Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her slave.
CSB17.30: Jacob slept with Rachel also, and indeed, he loved Rachel more than Leah. And he worked for Laban another seven years. <sup>ⓐ</sup>
CSB17.31: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, <sup>ⓑ</sup> he opened her womb; <sup>ⓒ</sup> but Rachel was unable to conceive. <sup>ⓓ</sup>
CSB17.32: Leah conceived, gave birth to a son, and named him Reuben, <sup>[8]</sup> for she said, “The LORD has seen my affliction; <sup>ⓔ</sup> surely my husband will love me now.”
CSB17.33: She conceived again, gave birth to a son, and said, “The LORD heard that I am unloved and has given me this son also.” So she named him Simeon. <sup>[9]</sup>
CSB17.34: She conceived again, gave birth to a son, and said, “At last, my husband will become attached to me because I have borne three sons for him.” Therefore he was named Levi. <sup>[10]</sup>
CSB17.35: And she conceived again, gave birth to a son, and said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” Therefore she named him Judah. <sup>[11]</sup> <sup>ⓕ</sup> Then Leah stopped having children.

WEB.1: Then Jacob went on his journey, and came to the land of the children of the east.
WEB.2: He looked, and behold, a well in the field, and, behold, three flocks of sheep lying there by it. For out of that well they watered the flocks. The stone on the well’s mouth was large.
WEB.3: There all the flocks were gathered. They rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the sheep, and put the stone again on the well’s mouth in its place.
WEB.4: Jacob said to them, “My relatives, where are you from?” They said, “We are from Haran.”
WEB.5: He said to them, “Do you know Laban, the son of Nahor?” They said, “We know him.”
WEB.6: He said to them, “Is it well with him?” They said, “It is well. See, Rachel, his daughter, is coming with the sheep.”
WEB.7: He said, “Behold, it is still the middle of the day, not time to gather the livestock together. Water the sheep, and go and feed them.”
WEB.8: They said, “We can’t, until all the flocks are gathered together, and they roll the stone from the well’s mouth. Then we water the sheep.”
WEB.9: While he was yet speaking with them, Rachel came with her father’s sheep, for she kept them.
WEB.10: When Jacob saw Rachel the daughter of Laban, his mother’s brother, and the sheep of Laban, his mother’s brother, Jacob went near, and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of Laban his mother’s brother.
WEB.11: Jacob kissed Rachel, and lifted up his voice, and wept.
WEB.12: Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s brother, and that he was Rebekah’s son. She ran and told her father.
WEB.13: When Laban heard the news of Jacob, his sister’s son, he ran to meet Jacob, and embraced him, and kissed him, and brought him to his house. Jacob told Laban all these things.
WEB.14: Laban said to him, “Surely you are my bone and my flesh.” He lived with him for a month.
WEB.15: Laban said to Jacob, “Because you are my brother, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what will your wages be?”
WEB.16: Laban had two daughters. The name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
WEB.17: Leah’s eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and attractive.
WEB.18: Jacob loved Rachel. He said, “I will serve you seven years for Rachel, your younger daughter.”
WEB.19: Laban said, “It is better that I give her to you, than that I should give her to another man. Stay with me.”
WEB.20: Jacob served seven years for Rachel. They seemed to him but a few days, for the love he had for her.
WEB.21: Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in to her.”
WEB.22: Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast.
WEB.23: In the evening, he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him. He went in to her.
WEB.24: Laban gave Zilpah his servant to his daughter Leah for a servant.
WEB.25: In the morning, behold, it was Leah. He said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? Didn’t I serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?”
WEB.26: Laban said, “It is not done so in our place, to give the younger before the firstborn.
WEB.27: Fulfill the week of this one, and we will give you the other also for the service which you will serve with me yet seven other years.”
WEB.28: Jacob did so, and fulfilled her week. He gave him Rachel his daughter as wife.
WEB.29: Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah, his servant, to be her servant.
WEB.30: He went in also to Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him yet seven other years.
WEB.31: Yahweh saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.
WEB.32: Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben. For she said, “Because Yahweh has looked at my affliction. For now my husband will love me.”
WEB.33: She conceived again, and bore a son, and said, “Because Yahweh has heard that I am hated, he has therefore given me this son also.” She named him Simeon.
WEB.34: She conceived again, and bore a son. Said, “Now this time will my husband be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore his name was called Levi.
WEB.35: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “This time will I praise Yahweh.” Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.

AMP.1: Then Jacob went on his way and came to the land of the people of the East [near Haran].
AMP.2: As he looked, he saw a well in the field, and three flocks of sheep lying there [resting] beside it because the flocks were watered from that well. Now the stone on the mouth of the well [that covered and protected it] was large,
AMP.3: and when all the flocks were gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone from the mouth of the well, water the sheep, and [afterward] replace the stone on the mouth of the well.
AMP.4: Jacob said to them, "My brothers, where are you from?" And they said, "We are from Haran."
AMP.5: So he said to them, "Do you know Laban the grandson of Nahor [Abraham's brother]?" And they replied, "We know him."
AMP.6: And he asked them, " Is it well with him?" And they said, "He is doing well; look, here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep!"
AMP.7: Jacob said, "Look, the sun is still high [overhead]; it is a long time before the flocks need to be gathered [in their folds for the night]. Water the sheep, and go, and return them to their pasture."
AMP.8: But they said, "We cannot [leave] until all the flocks are gathered together, and the shepherds roll the stone from the mouth of the well; then we will water the sheep."
AMP.9: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel came with her father's sheep, for she was a shepherdess.
AMP.10: When Jacob saw [his cousin] Rachel, the daughter of Laban, his mother's brother, and Laban's sheep, he came up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered the flock of Laban, his uncle.
AMP.11: Then Jacob kissed Rachel [in greeting], and he raised his voice and wept.
AMP.12: Jacob told Rachel he was her father's relative, Rebekah's son; and she ran and told her father.
AMP.13: When Laban heard of the arrival of Jacob, his sister's son, he ran to meet him, and embraced and kissed him and brought him to his house. Then he told Laban all these things.
AMP.14: Then Laban said to him, "You are my bone and my flesh." And Jacob stayed with him a month.
AMP.15: Then Laban said to Jacob, "Just because you are my relative, should you work for me for nothing? Tell me, what should your wages be?"
AMP.16: Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the older was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
AMP.17: Leah's eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and appearance.
AMP.18: Jacob loved Rachel, so he said, "I will serve you [as a hired workman] for seven years [in return] for [the privilege of marrying] Rachel your younger daughter."
AMP.19: Laban said, "It is better that I give her [in marriage] to you than give her to another man. Stay and work with me."
AMP.20: So Jacob served [Laban] for seven years for [the right to marry] Rachel, but they seemed like only a few days to him because of his love for her.
AMP.21: Finally, Jacob said to Laban, "Give me my wife, for my time [of service] is completed, so that I may take her to me [as my wife]."
AMP.22: So Laban gathered together all the men of the place and prepared a [wedding] feast [with wine].
AMP.23: But in the evening he took Leah his daughter and brought her to Jacob, and Jacob went in to [consummate the marriage with] her.
AMP.24: Laban also gave Zilpah his maid to his daughter Leah as a maid.
AMP.25: But in the morning [when Jacob awoke], it was Leah [who was with him]! And he said to Laban, "What is this that you have done to me? Did I not work for you [for seven years] for Rachel? Why have you deceived and betrayed me [like this]?"
AMP.26: But Laban only said, "It is not the tradition here to give the younger [daughter in marriage] before the older.
AMP.27: Finish the week [of the wedding feast] for Leah; then we will give you Rachel also, and in return you shall work for me for seven more years."
AMP.28: So Jacob complied and fulfilled Leah's week [of celebration]; then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as his [second] wife.
AMP.29: Laban also gave Bilhah his maid to his daughter Rachel as a maid.
AMP.30: So Jacob consummated his marriage and lived with Rachel [as his wife], and he loved Rachel more than Leah, and he served with Laban for another seven years.
AMP.31: Now when the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He made her able to bear children, but Rachel was barren.
AMP.32: Leah conceived and gave birth to a son and named him Reuben (See, a son!), for she said, "Because the LORD has seen my humiliation and suffering; now my husband will love me [since I have given him a son]."
AMP.33: Then she conceived again and gave birth to a son and said, "Because the LORD heard that I am unloved, He has given me this son also." So she named him Simeon (God hears).
AMP.34: She conceived again and gave birth to a son and said, "Now this time my husband will become attached to me [as a companion], for I have given him three sons." Therefore he was named Levi.
AMP.35: Again she conceived and gave birth to a [fourth] son, and she said, "Now I will praise the LORD." So she named him Judah; then [for a time] she stopped bearing [children].

MSG.1: Jacob set out again on his way to the people of the east.
MSG.2: He noticed a well out in an open field with three flocks of sheep bedded down around it. This was the common well from which the flocks were watered. The stone over the mouth of the well was huge.
MSG.3: When all the flocks were gathered, the shepherds would roll the stone from the well and water the sheep; then they would return the stone, covering the well.
MSG.4:
Jacob said, "Hello friends. Where are you from?"
They said, "We're from Haran."
MSG.5:
Jacob asked, "Do you know Laban son of Nahor?"
"We do."
MSG.6:
"Are things well with him?" Jacob continued.
"Very well," they said. "And here is his daughter Rachel coming with the flock."
MSG.7: Jacob said, "There's a lot of daylight still left; it isn't time to round up the sheep yet, is it? So why not water the flocks and go back to grazing?"
MSG.8: "We can't," they said. "Not until all the shepherds get here. It takes all of us to roll the stone from the well. Not until then can we water the flocks."
MSG.9: While Jacob was in conversation with them, Rachel came up with her father's sheep. She was the shepherd.

MSG.11: Then he kissed Rachel and broke into tears.
MSG.12: He told Rachel that he was related to her father, that he was Rebekah's son. She ran and told her father.
MSG.13: When Laban heard the news—Jacob, his sister's son!—he ran out to meet him, embraced and kissed him and brought him home. Jacob told Laban the story of everything that had happened.
MSG.14:
Laban said, "You're family! My flesh and blood!"
When Jacob had been with him for a month,
MSG.15: Laban said, "Just because you're my nephew, you shouldn't work for me for nothing. Tell me what you want to be paid. What's a fair wage?"
MSG.16: Now Laban had two daughters; Leah was the older and Rachel the younger.
MSG.17: Leah had nice eyes, but Rachel was stunningly beautiful.
MSG.18:

MSG.29: (Laban gave his maid Bilhah to his daughter Rachel as her maid.)

MSG.31: When God realized that Leah was unloved, he opened her womb. But Rachel was barren.

MSG.35: She became pregnant a final time and had a fourth son. She said, "This time I'll praise God." So she named him Judah (Praise-God). Then she stopped having children.

NRSVCE.10: Now when Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his mother’s brother Laban, and the sheep of his mother’s brother Laban, Jacob went up and rolled the stone from the well’s mouth, and watered the flock of his mother’s brother Laban.

NRSVCE.12: And Jacob told Rachel that he was her father’s kinsman, and that he was Rebekah’s son; and she ran and told her father.
NRSVCE.13: When Laban heard the news about his sister’s son Jacob, he ran to meet him; he embraced him and kissed him, and brought him to his house. Jacob told Laban all these things,
NRSVCE.14: and Laban said to him, “Surely you are my bone and my flesh!” And he stayed with him a month.
NRSVCE.15: Then Laban said to Jacob, “Because you are my kinsman, should you therefore serve me for nothing? Tell me, what shall your wages be?”
NRSVCE.16: Now Laban had two daughters; the name of the elder was Leah, and the name of the younger was Rachel.
NRSVCE.17: Leah’s eyes were lovely, and Rachel was graceful and beautiful.
NRSVCE.18: Jacob loved Rachel; so he said, “I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.”
NRSVCE.19: Laban said, “It is better that I give her to you than that I should give her to any other man; stay with me.”
NRSVCE.20: So Jacob served seven years for Rachel, and they seemed to him but a few days because of the love he had for her.
NRSVCE.21: Then Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife that I may go in to her, for my time is completed.”
NRSVCE.22: So Laban gathered together all the people of the place, and made a feast.
NRSVCE.23: But in the evening he took his daughter Leah and brought her to Jacob; and he went in to her.
NRSVCE.24: (Laban gave his maid Zilpah to his daughter Leah to be her maid.)
NRSVCE.25: When morning came, it was Leah! And Jacob said to Laban, “What is this you have done to me? Did I not serve with you for Rachel? Why then have you deceived me?”
NRSVCE.26: Laban said, “This is not done in our country — giving the younger before the firstborn.
NRSVCE.27: Complete the week of this one, and we will give you the other also in return for serving me another seven years.”
NRSVCE.28: Jacob did so, and completed her week; then Laban gave him his daughter Rachel as a wife.
NRSVCE.29: (Laban gave his maid Bilhah to his daughter Rachel to be her maid.)
NRSVCE.30: So Jacob went in to Rachel also, and he loved Rachel more than Leah. He served Laban for another seven years.
NRSVCE.31: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, he opened her womb; but Rachel was barren.
NRSVCE.32: Leah conceived and bore a son, and she named him Reuben; for she said, “Because the LORD has looked on my affliction; surely now my husband will love me.”
NRSVCE.33: She conceived again and bore a son, and said, “Because the LORD has heard that I am hated, he has given me this son also”; and she named him Simeon.
NRSVCE.34: Again she conceived and bore a son, and said, “Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons”; therefore he was named Levi.
NRSVCE.35: She conceived again and bore a son, and said, “This time I will praise the LORD”; therefore she named him Judah; then she ceased bearing.

NET.1: So Jacob moved on and came to the land of the eastern people.
NET.2: He saw in the field a well with three flocks of sheep lying beside it, because the flocks were watered from that well. Now a large stone covered the mouth of the well.
NET.3: When all the flocks were gathered there, the shepherds would roll the stone off the mouth of the well and water the sheep. Then they would put the stone back in its place over the well’s mouth.
NET.4: Jacob asked them, “My brothers, where are you from?” They replied, “We’re from Haran.”
NET.5: So he said to them, “Do you know Laban, the grandson of Nahor?” “We know him,” they said.
NET.6: “Is he well?” Jacob asked. They replied, “He is well. Now look, here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
NET.7: Then Jacob said, “Since it is still the middle of the day, it is not time for the flocks to be gathered. You should water the sheep and then go and let them graze some more.”
NET.8: “We can’t,” they said, “until all the flocks are gathered and the stone is rolled off the mouth of the well. Then we water the sheep.”
NET.9: While he was still speaking with them, Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep, for she was tending them.
NET.10: When Jacob saw Rachel, the daughter of his uncle Laban, and the sheep of his uncle Laban, he went over and rolled the stone off the mouth of the well and watered the sheep of his uncle Laban.
NET.11: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and began to weep loudly.
NET.12: When Jacob explained to Rachel that he was a relative of her father and the son of Rebekah, she ran and told her father.
NET.13: When Laban heard this news about Jacob, his sister’s son, he rushed out to meet him. He embraced him and kissed him and brought him to his house. Jacob told Laban how he was related to him.
NET.14: Then Laban said to him, “You are indeed my own flesh and blood.” So Jacob stayed with him for a month.
NET.15: Then Laban said to Jacob, “Should you work for me for nothing because you are my relative? Tell me what your wages should be.”
NET.16: (Now Laban had two daughters; the older one was named Leah, and the younger one Rachel.
NET.17: Leah’s eyes were tender, but Rachel had a lovely figure and beautiful appearance.)
NET.18: Since Jacob had fallen in love with Rachel, he said, “I’ll serve you seven years in exchange for your younger daughter Rachel.”
NET.19: Laban replied, “I’d rather give her to you than to another man. Stay with me.”
NET.20: So Jacob worked for seven years to acquire Rachel. But they seemed like only a few days to him because his love for her was so great.
NET.21: Finally Jacob said to Laban, “Give me my wife, for my time of service is up. I want to have marital relations with her.”
NET.22: So Laban invited all the people of that place and prepared a feast.
NET.23: In the evening he brought his daughter Leah to Jacob, and Jacob had marital relations with her.
NET.24: (Laban gave his female servant Zilpah to his daughter Leah to be her servant.)
NET.25: In the morning Jacob discovered it was Leah! So Jacob said to Laban, “What in the world have you done to me! Didn’t I work for you in exchange for Rachel? Why have you tricked me?”
NET.26: “It is not our custom here,” Laban replied, “to give the younger daughter in marriage before the firstborn.
NET.27: Complete my older daughter’s bridal week. Then we will give you the younger one too, in exchange for seven more years of work.”
NET.28: Jacob did as Laban said. When Jacob completed Leah’s bridal week, Laban gave him his daughter Rachel to be his wife.
NET.29: (Laban gave his female servant Bilhah to his daughter Rachel to be her servant.)
NET.30: Jacob had marital relations with Rachel as well. He loved Rachel more than Leah, so he worked for Laban for seven more years.
NET.31: When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, he enabled her to become pregnant while Rachel remained childless.
NET.32: So Leah became pregnant and gave birth to a son. She named him Reuben, for she said, “The LORD has looked with pity on my oppressed condition. Surely my husband will love me now.”
NET.33: She became pregnant again and had another son. She said, “Because the LORD heard that I was unloved, he gave me this one too.” So she named him Simeon.
NET.34: She became pregnant again and had another son. She said, “Now this time my husband will show me affection, because I have given birth to three sons for him.” That is why he was named Levi.
NET.35: She became pregnant again and had another son. She said, “This time I will praise the LORD.” That is why she named him Judah. Then she stopped having children.
